task.title: The vocabulary placeholder is clipped where it matters most
task.description:
When a task's status or priority is one this project's vocabulary cannot resolve, the web board's detail form shows a placeholder instead of selecting the wrong thing. The placeholder reads:

    Choose one of this project's statuses (current: ready)

The properties column is about 200px wide, so what a person actually sees, collapsed, is:

    Choose one of this pro...

The useful half is the half that is cut off. The instruction is generic and could be guessed from context; the value in parentheses is the one fact the reader cannot get anywhere else on the card, because the chip renders the raw token with nothing marking it as stranded.

## Where it is

showStatus and statusPlaceholder in internal/webui/assets/index.html, around line 2470, and the priority twins showPriority/priorityPlaceholder added beside them. Both halves word it the same way, so both are clipped the same way. This was found while adding the priority half; the status half has behaved like this for as long as the placeholder has existed.

## Not broken, just useless at a glance

Opening the select shows the full text, so nothing is unrecoverable. A reader who notices something is odd can find out what. The cost is that they have to notice and then act, when the point of a placeholder is to say what is wrong without being asked.

## What to consider

Lead with the value rather than the instruction — something along the lines of 'Current: ready (not in this project)' puts the unrecoverable fact first and lets the clip take the explanatory half. Check it against the real column width in both the task detail and wherever else the select is rendered, and in both color schemes, rather than counting characters.

While there: nothing outside the select marks a stranded value at all. A priority chip reads CRITICAL exactly as a live one would. Statuses get a whole unknown region on the board, which is the precedent for saying so somewhere visible; priorities have no equivalent. Worth deciding whether they should, and it is a separate question from the clipping.

## Fix both halves together

They are the same wording in two places. Fixing one and not the other leaves the board saying the same thing two different ways about two vocabularies that are otherwise deliberately symmetric.
